article_content: The dismissal of the €145m case against Juan Carlos, the former king of Spain, by a London court has sparked varied reactions. Corinna zu Sayn-Wittgenstein-Sayn, who accused him of harassment, expressed disappointment, while Juan Carlos's team saw it as a vindication of his innocence. The case, filed in 2020, alleged that Juan Carlos orchestrated a campaign of intimidation, including spying and break-ins, after their relationship ended in 2012. Juan Carlos consistently denied these allegations. The court's ruling was based on the lack of jurisdiction, without making a judgment on the substance of the claims. This decision comes after UK judges previously ruled that Juan Carlos had immunity as a sovereign, preventing him from being sued over actions during his reign. The former king has been living in exile since 2020, following various scandals and allegations of fraud.
